dedupe_keys.name: a global database of porphyry copper deposits and prospects usgs 2025

description: This U.S. Geological Survey data release compiles and updates earlier global and regional datasets of porphyry copper deposits and prospects, the world's main source of copper and a host of by-product critical minerals. The ScienceBase page says the data sheet gives deposit names and locations, age with the analytical method where known, a deposit class based on Hofstra and others (2021), the interpreted tectonic origin and grade and tonnage from public databases where available, current as of spring 2024. It was published on 4 March 2025 by Benjamin Magnin, Garth Graham, David Huston and Bruce Eglington as a CSV data sheet of about 0.95 MB with a data dictionary, a references PDF and metadata, downloadable and free under CC0 1.0. Coverage is global. Caveats: grade and tonnage are filled only where public figures exist, prospects are mixed with deposits, and the number of records is not stated on the page read. For simulation it maps the global copper supply base, useful for supply chain and price shock scenarios for grids, electrification and electronics, and for hazard exposure of mining regions along plate margins. Related catalogue records include the USGS global critical minerals distribution, the WAPHA global metal mines database and the BGS World Mineral Statistics.
name: A global database of porphyry copper deposits and prospects (USGS, 2025)
